definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Granola__get_meeting_transcript
definition.description:
Get the verbatim transcript of a Granola meeting by ID; no summaries or notes.
Returns up to 40000 characters per call by default (max_chars, up to 80000), cut at an utterance boundary with total_chars, truncated and next_offset reported. A page that splits an oversized utterance has ends_mid_utterance and the next starts_mid_utterance.
With meeting_ids, meetings has one entry per requested ID in request order, with the single-read fields or an error. The batch shares 80000 characters: each meeting returns up to max_chars or an equal share of that, whichever is smaller. Pass offsets to continue several meetings in one call.
An accessible meeting with no transcript returns transcript null (status "unavailable" for chunk reads) and transcript_unavailable with a reason: transcript_pending means retry in a few minutes; not_happened_yet means retry after the meeting; no_transcript and transcript_deleted are final. "Meeting not found" means the ID does not resolve or is not accessible.
Transcript blocks separate audio source (Microphone/System audio) from speaker identity; mobile/imported transcripts may keep Speaker A/B labels. For native recordings, recording context identifies the document owner as the recorder, not necessarily the speaker; missing recorder data stays unknown.
Needs a paid Granola plan. If it returns a paid-plan error, use the other meeting tools and say when their results lack the requested detail.

meeting_ids.description: Meeting UUIDs or public note IDs (max 10). With several IDs, offset applies to each meeting and the meetings share 80000 characters, so each returns up to max_chars or an equal share, whichever is smaller; use offsets to start meetings at different positions. A meeting that cannot be read gets an error entry and the others are still returned. Empty arrays are ignored.

note_ids.description: Alias for meeting_ids. If both are nonempty, they must refer to the same set of notes; order, duplicates, and UUID/public ID format may differ.

meeting_id.description: Alias for meeting_ids with a single meeting. Every ID argument provided must name the same meetings.

note_id.description: Alias for meeting_ids with a single meeting. Every ID argument provided must name the same meetings.

offset.description: Character offset; pass next_offset to continue, with the same include_timestamps as that page.

max_chars.description: Maximum size of the transcript field as sent (integer, at least 1,000), cut at the last utterance that fits; a page holds fewer transcript characters when the text needs JSON escaping. Defaults to 40000; larger requests are capped at 80000. Use next_offset to continue. Lower it if responses exceed your output limit.

include_timestamps.description: Prefix each reliably timed block with [m:ss], minutes:seconds since the transcript's earliest timed block, not clock time; that block can predate the meeting when recording started early. Applies to every page; chunk_ids reads always include them. Adds about 7 characters per block, and offset, next_offset and total_chars count the text as rendered with it, so keep the same value when continuing from next_offset. When no block has timing, no prefixes are added and timestamps_unavailable says so.

offsets.description: With meeting_ids only: character offset per meeting, keyed by meeting ID, e.g. {"<id>": 8000}. Pass each truncated meeting's next_offset to continue several transcripts in one call. Meetings not listed start at offset. Omit or pass {} when not needed.

chunk_ids.description: Read up to ten finalized transcript chunks instead of the full transcript. Use chunk IDs from search_transcripts, or [0] to browse from the beginning. IDs past the last chunk are skipped and listed in ignored_chunk_ids; if none of the IDs exist the status is out_of_range. Each chunk's transcript is verbatim text in the full read's format: one block per speaker turn, prefixed with [m:ss] (minutes:seconds since the transcript's earliest timed block, omitted when unknown) and the speaker label; preformatted transcripts keep their own text and labels. Also returns total_chunks and previous/next chunk IDs.

transcript_version.description: With chunk_ids, reuse the version from search or a previous chunk read. A changed status returns no chunks: search again or restart browsing without the old version. Omit chunk_ids and transcript_version for the existing full transcript read.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Granola__get_meetings
definition.description:
Read one or more Granola meetings by ID: private notes, AI summary, attendees, metadata and note URLs. Use it when you have meeting IDs from discovery results or note URLs; batch up to 10 IDs per call.
Private notes appear only for meetings the user owns (status "empty": no text; "not_included": another user owns the note).
meeting_at is the calendar event's scheduled start (created_at without an event), so it can differ from when the meeting was recorded.
Invalid, missing and inaccessible IDs are reported separately; the other meetings are still returned.
If the meetings would exceed 80000 characters, the last ones are left out and listed in omitted_meetings; read them in another call.
The note creator and participants are not necessarily the connected user: confirm the connected user's identity with get_account_info and match it to explicit ownership evidence before drafting in the user's voice or assigning them actions; first-person notes are not proof of the user's voice. Dated plans do not establish current progress.
known_participants comes from the calendar invite, attendees added by hand, and the note creator; anyone else who spoke appears only in the notes and transcript.
Does not return transcripts; notes can omit details that were discussed. If a detail is missing, get_meeting_transcript may have it on a paid Granola plan; if it returns a paid-plan error, say the detail is missing rather than conclude it was never discussed.
Shared-screen screenshots appear in <attachments> with an ID, time offset and lossy description; for anything visual (designs, slides, charts, code), view them with get_meeting_attachment.
Attached photos appear as <attachment type="photo"> without a description; view them with get_meeting_attachment.
Keep at most 5 get_meetings calls in flight, and only for calls you already need. On a rate_limit error, retry only the failed call after retry_after_seconds, one at a time, and not when retryable is false.

meeting_ids.description: Meeting UUIDs, public note IDs (not_...) or upcoming-meeting IDs (evt_...) (max 10). Provide at least one ID in meeting_ids or note_ids; empty arrays are ignored.

note_ids.description: Alias for meeting_ids. Empty arrays are ignored. If both are nonempty, they must refer to the same set of notes; order, duplicates, and UUID/public ID format may differ.

max_participants.description: Maximum attendees to list per meeting, besides the note creator. Omit to list everyone. Set a small value (e.g. 10) for broad ranges or large meetings to keep responses small. When attendees are left out, known_participants has total and omitted attributes, e.g. <known_participants total="250" omitted="240">.

attachments.description: Omit or pass "list" to list each meeting's viewable attachments with their IDs; when several meetings are returned, only the first 20 per meeting are listed and the attachments element says how many were left out. Pass "count" to get only an attachment_count attribute on each meeting that has attachments. Pass "none" to leave attachments out.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Granola__query_granola_meetings
definition.description:
Query Granola about the user's meetings in natural language. Returns an answer with inline markdown citation links (e.g. [[1]](url)) to the source meeting notes; keep them in your response so the user can verify it. The citation URL https://notes.granola.ai/d/<meeting_id> gives the ID to pass to get_meetings (meeting_ids).

The answer is a summary that can leave out owners, numbers, dates and exact wording; when the question asks for those, read the cited meetings with get_meetings first.

This tool is slow: an agent behind it searches and reads the user's notes. Prefer a faster tool when it can answer:
- Meeting discovery tools: find meetings by date range
- get_meetings: read notes for meetings whose IDs you already have
- search_meetings: find meetings by keyword, participant or company

Use it for what was discussed, decided or assigned across meetings, follow-ups and commitments, or when the user references their 'Granola notes'.

When NOT to use:
- Scheduling meetings or changing calendar invites
- A specific meeting by ID: use get_meetings

Transcripts need a paid Granola plan. If get_meeting_transcript returns a paid-plan error and results lack a detail, say so rather than conclude it was never discussed.
Keep at most 15 query_granola_meetings calls in flight, and only for calls you already need. On a rate_limit error, retry only the failed call after retry_after_seconds, one at a time, and not when retryable is false.

query.description: The query to run on Granola meeting notes

document_ids.description: Optional meeting UUIDs or public note IDs to limit context to (max 10).

items.description: Meeting UUID, public note ID (not_...) or Granola note link

note_ids.description: Alias for document_ids (max 10). If both are provided, they must refer to the same set of notes; order, duplicates, and UUID/public ID format may differ.

items.description: Meeting UUID, public note ID (not_...) or Granola note link

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Granola__search_meetings
definition.description:
Find the user's meetings by keyword, participant/company, date, or a combination. Keyword searches cover meeting titles, summaries and your private notes. They do not search transcripts: an empty result does not mean a term was never spoken in a meeting. Returns metadata only (title, date, participants, note headings), not what was said: read the relevant meetings with get_meetings before answering about their content, and use get_meetings directly for a meeting you already identified. With keywords or participant, results are ranked by relevance favouring recent meetings; with neither, newest first, defaulting to the last 7 days.

Pass next_cursor as cursor with the same filters to continue; pages can be short or empty, so continue while next_cursor is present. completion_status incomplete means continuation is unavailable: narrow the search.

When the searched dates reach past now, the first page starts with upcoming_meetings (not part of cursor pagination): up to limit (at most 50) matching calendar meetings in the next 14 days, soonest first, matched on their titles, attendees and organizer, and the user's notes for them. Each is listed only there until it ends or is summarized, under an evt_ ID that works as a meeting ID in other tools. When more match, it has next_from: call again with from_date set to it.

participant matches participant metadata (names, emails, companies, domains), not mentions in notes, as an AND filter with the other inputs; metadata can be incomplete. For broader questions about a person or company, also search their name plus the topic in keywords with participant omitted: internal discussions may hold the answer.

Captures of the same calendar event are grouped, keeping the user's own note or else the newest; read other_ids in duplicate_recordings only for details the listed note lacks or when the user asks to compare attendees' notes. Use attended_only=true for 'my meetings'. list_meeting_folders gives folder_id values. Keyword matching is literal, so pass the user's words plus obvious synonyms. Meetings with viewable attachments carry an attachment_count attribute; get_meetings lists them.
Keep at most 2 search_meetings calls in flight, and only for calls you already need. On a rate_limit error, retry only the failed call after retry_after_seconds, one at a time, and not when retryable is false.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous response. Omit filters to reuse them, or repeat the same filters. Omit cursor or pass an empty string for the first page. Cursors expire after 15 minutes.

folder_id.description: Only return meetings in this folder or its nested folders. Use list_meeting_folders to discover folder IDs.

workspace_only.description: Set to true only when the user explicitly asks for Team Space, public workspace, or workspace-visible meetings. Omit or set to false to search every meeting the user is allowed to access. Combines with folder_id and include_shared using AND.

keywords.description: Groups of words to search for in meeting titles, summaries, or your private notes. Transcript text is not searched. All words in one entry must appear within the same field, in any order or position. Entries are alternatives (OR): ["MCP write tools"] requires all three words; ["write tools", "write access"] matches either group. Pass at most 20 entries. Adjacent words in the supplied order get a relevance boost, but exact phrases are not required. A single comma-separated string is also accepted. Omit to browse meetings by date.

max_participants.description: Maximum attendees to list per meeting, besides the note creator. Omit to list everyone. Set a small value (e.g. 10) for broad ranges or large meetings to keep responses small. When attendees are left out, known_participants has total and omitted attributes, e.g. <known_participants total="250" omitted="240">.

participant.description: Filter meetings with a participant name, email, company name, or domain in participant metadata. Combines with keywords, dates, and folder using AND. Mentions in notes alone do not match; missing participant metadata can hide relevant meetings. For broader questions about their work, account status, decisions, issue resolution, or preparation, also search the person/company and topic in keywords without this filter to include internal discussions.

limit.description: Requested meetings per page (positive integer). Defaults to 30 and is capped at 100. Larger requests use the cap; use next_cursor to continue. Duplicates or inaccessible matches can make a page shorter.

attended_only.description: Only notes the user captured or where their email is listed as a creator or attendee. Approximates attendance; defaults to false.

include_shared.description: Also search notes other people shared with the user. Defaults to true when omitted.

from_date.description: Only meetings on or after this ISO date or time, using calendar start when available, otherwise note creation. Dates and offsetless times use the user's timezone (UTC if unavailable); explicit offsets are respected, so for a day in another timezone give both bounds as times with that timezone's offset.

to_date.description: Only meetings on or before this ISO date or time. YYYY-MM-DD includes the whole day in the user's timezone (UTC if unavailable); explicit offsets are respected. Uses calendar start when available, otherwise note creation.

updated_after.description: Only notes whose summary or content changed after this ISO date or time; matching rows then show updated_at. Use it to pick up changes since a previous call. Combines with the other filters using AND; without from_date and to_date it covers all accessible meeting history (the last 30 days on the free plan) instead of the last 7 days. Offsetless values use the user's timezone (UTC if unavailable).

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Granola__search_transcripts
definition.description:
Find specific words or quotes in accessible meeting transcripts in the active workspace. Returns ranked passages with approximate timestamps.

Needs a paid Granola plan. If it returns a paid-plan error, use the other meeting tools.

Supply meeting_ids when known, batching meetings that share the same terms and filters. Matching is literal; put alternative words in one keywords array, e.g. ["pricing", "price", "cost"]. For what a person or company said, use participant (names/companies) or attendee_emails/attendee_domains (invite list). participant is an AND filter on metadata that can be incomplete, so for broader questions also search their name and the topic in keywords without it.

Known meetings with no indexed match are also searched in their current transcripts. Without meeting_ids, search relies on an asynchronously updated index and groups duplicate recordings; empty results do not prove a topic was never discussed.

Follow next_cursor even on empty pages, passing only cursor and optionally limit. If completion_status is incomplete, narrow the search or read known transcripts.

Read surrounding dialogue with get_meeting_transcript using meeting_id, the passage's chunk_ids and transcript_version; adjacent chunk IDs continue, and omitting chunk_ids reads the whole conversation.

counts is cumulative across pages; total_matching_chunks is a first-page estimate, null for direct search. Neither counts spoken mentions.

Use another tool when:
- The term is likely in the notes, or the user wants meetings about a topic: use search_meetings
- You need the whole conversation: use get_meeting_transcript

keywords.description: Required for a new search. Entries are alternatives (OR); all words within an entry must occur in one chunk, in any order. Accepts an array or comma-separated string.

meeting_ids.description: Restrict to these meetings (UUIDs or public note IDs, max 100). Batch IDs sharing the same terms and filters. Omit to search all accessible indexed meetings.

items.description: Meeting UUID, public note ID (not_...) or Granola note link

cursor.description: Pass next_cursor from a previous result; only limit may accompany it. Omit or pass an empty string for the first page. Cursors expire after 15 minutes.

limit.description: Passages per page with meeting_ids; otherwise meetings per page. Default 10, capped at 20.

from_date.description: Only meetings on or after this ISO date or time, using calendar start when available, otherwise note creation. Dates and offsetless times use the user's timezone (UTC if unavailable).

to_date.description: Only meetings on or before this ISO date or time. YYYY-MM-DD includes the whole day in the user's timezone (UTC if unavailable). Uses calendar start when available, otherwise note creation.

participant.description: Filter by participant name, email, company name, or domain in meeting participant metadata. Combines with keywords, dates, meeting_ids, attendee_emails, and attendee_domains using AND. Mentions in the transcript alone do not match. Missing participant metadata can hide relevant meetings; metadata does not prove attendance.

attendee_emails.description: Only meetings whose invite list includes any of these emails, e.g. ["alice@acme.com"]

attendee_domains.description: Only meetings whose invite list includes anyone at these email domains, including subdomains, e.g. ["acme.com"]

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Cloudflare Developer Platform
DEPRECATED: This Workers Bindings MCP server is deprecated. Use the Cloudflare API MCP server at https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp instead. It covers the full Cloudflare API, including Workers Bindings.

## claude.ai Gamma
Gamma creates AI-powered presentations, documents, webpages, and social posts. Only include optional parameters when the user explicitly requests or clearly implies them. Gamma has intelligent defaults - when in doubt, omit. When uncertain about user preferences, ask rather than assume. The read_gamma tool can read the content of an existing Gamma when given its file ID. Existing gammas have a type: "template" or "regular". Only templates can be used with generate_from_template; discover valid templates with get_gammas(type="template") or the workspaceTemplates list from search_templates. Non-template IDs and search_templates exploreTemplates IDs are not valid inputs to generate_from_template. If generate_from_template reports that an ID is inaccessible or not a template, find a valid template with get_gammas(type="template") or search_templates (workspaceTemplates only). If the user's intent is to create a new gamma, but not by using an existing template, then use the generate tool. Limits in these tool schemas and in failed results (card count, image models, credits) reflect the workspace's current Gamma plan. When a request exceeds one of them, tell the user which limit applies; do not promise a specific higher limit. If edit_gamma is available in the tool list, use it to modify an existing gamma with a natural-language instruction. If edit_gamma is not available, let the user know they can customize their gamma directly in the Gamma editor.

## claude.ai Granola
Granola is an AI notepad for meetings. Use its tools to answer questions about the user's past meetings, notes, decisions, and action items. Before answering about what was said, decided or assigned in a specific meeting, read that meeting with get_meetings: search results and meeting lists can leave out owners, numbers and exact wording. Transcripts need a paid Granola plan. If get_meeting_transcript returns a paid-plan error and results lack a detail, say so rather than conclude it was never discussed. """Container and Supabase coverage tests for the deploy-secret-allowlist lint.

Split out of test_lint_deploy_secret_allowlist.py, which crossed the R29
500-line ceiling. The Cloudflare-worker cases stayed there; the container and
edge-function coverage cases live here. Shared scaffolding comes from
deploy_secret_allowlist_support so the two halves cannot drift.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from deploy_secret_allowlist_support import build_tree, load_lint

# ── Container coverage tests ─────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _make_container_dir(tree: Path, name: str) -> Path:
    """Create a container dir with a coolify/docker-compose.yaml."""
    compose = tree / f"infra/containers/python/{name}/coolify/docker-compose.yaml"
    compose.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    compose.write_text(f"services:\n  {name}:\n    image: {name}\n")
    return compose


def test_container_with_compose_but_no_manifest_entry(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    """A container with a compose file but no manifest section has no delivery path."""
    tree = build_tree(
        tmp_path,
        staging_allow=["CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY"],
        production_allow=["CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY", "WORKER_REQ", "WORKER_OPT"],
        website_keys=["WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY"],
        worker_required=["WORKER_REQ"],
        worker_keys=["WORKER_REQ", "WORKER_OPT"],
    )
    _make_container_dir(tree, "my-container")
    assert load_lint(tree).main() == 1
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert "[NO-MANIFEST-ENTRY] container 'my-container'" in err


def test_stale_container_manifest_entry_fails(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    """A docker manifest section for a container with no compose file is stale."""
    tree = build_tree(
        tmp_path,
        staging_allow=["CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY"],
        production_allow=["CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY", "WORKER_REQ", "WORKER_OPT"],
        website_keys=["WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY"],
        worker_required=["WORKER_REQ"],
        worker_keys=["WORKER_REQ", "WORKER_OPT"],
    )
    manifest = tree / "workers/secrets.toml"
    manifest.write_text(
        manifest.read_text()
        + '\n[ghost-container]\ndeploy_type = "docker"\nrequired = []\nkeys = ["GHOST_KEY"]\n'
    )
    assert load_lint(tree).main() == 1
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert "[STALE-MANIFEST-ENTRY] [ghost-container]" in err


def test_docker_section_secrets_not_checked_against_allowlist(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    """Container secrets are documentation-only; they are NOT on the deploy allowlist.

    The allowlist check only applies to cloudflare sections. A docker section
    with secrets that are not on the allowlist must NOT trigger a drift finding.
    """
    tree = build_tree(
        tmp_path,
        staging_allow=["CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY"],
        production_allow=["CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY", "WORKER_REQ", "WORKER_OPT"],
        website_keys=["WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY"],
        worker_required=["WORKER_REQ"],
        worker_keys=["WORKER_REQ", "WORKER_OPT"],
    )
    _make_container_dir(tree, "my-container")
    manifest = tree / "workers/secrets.toml"
    manifest.write_text(
        manifest.read_text()
        + '\n[my-container]\ndeploy_type = "docker"\nrequired = []\nkeys = ["CONTAINER_SECRET"]\n'
    )
    assert load_lint(tree).main() == 0


def test_container_with_deploy_prod_compose_detected(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    """Containers with deploy/docker-compose.prod.yaml (not coolify/) are found."""
    tree = build_tree(
        tmp_path,
        staging_allow=["CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY"],
        production_allow=["CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY", "WORKER_REQ", "WORKER_OPT"],
        website_keys=["WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY"],
        worker_required=["WORKER_REQ"],
        worker_keys=["WORKER_REQ", "WORKER_OPT"],
    )
    compose = tree / "infra/containers/infra/bifrost/deploy/docker-compose.prod.yaml"
    compose.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    compose.write_text("services:\n  bifrost:\n    image: bifrost\n")
    assert load_lint(tree).main() == 1
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert "[NO-MANIFEST-ENTRY] container 'bifrost'" in err


# ── Supabase coverage tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_supabase_function_without_manifest_entry(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    """A supabase function dir with index.ts but no manifest section is flagged."""
    tree = build_tree(
        tmp_path,
        staging_allow=["CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN", "WEBSITE_ONLY_KEY"],

# `critical-crons` on `ops` — cutover runbook

Moves the last hand-managed Coolify-era stack onto the pull-based
`vm-updater` (ETH-ux9qi), and takes its ~10 credentials out of a cleartext
compose file at the same time (ETH-mejqj).

Rotating without moving to an `env_file` writes fresh credentials straight back

"""Deployment guards for the alert-cooldown state directory (ETH-y2ve7).

The cooldown's correctness depends on infrastructure that no test touched: a
named volume so state outlives a Coolify redeploy, and a `chown` so the non-root
runtime user can write into that volume. Both are invisible to the Python suite,
and an adversarial review confirmed it: deleting the volume declaration left 27
tests green while production degraded to paging every tick, and deleting the
`chown` left everything green while the container crashed on `PermissionError`
every tick — a canary that is both loud and dead.

These are cheap file assertions, not integration tests. They exist so the
guard's supporting infrastructure cannot be removed silently.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import yaml

CONTAINERS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "python"
STATE_DIR = "/var/lib/monocloud"

# service directory -> (compose service name, volume name)
DEPLOYMENTS = {
    "critical-canaries": ("critical-canaries", "critical-canaries-state"),
    "critical-crons": ("critical-crons", "critical-crons-state"),
}


def _compose(service_dir: str) -> dict:
    path = CONTAINERS / service_dir / "coolify" / "docker-compose.yaml"
    return yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("service_dir", "wiring"), sorted(DEPLOYMENTS.items()))
def test_alert_state_lives_on_a_named_volume(service_dir: str, wiring: tuple[str, str]) -> None:
    """Coolify recreates the container on every deploy. Container-local state
    resets the cooldown on each ship and quietly restores the 96-a-day flood —
    and every Python test still passes, because none of them deploy anything."""
    service_name, volume = wiring
    compose = _compose(service_dir)
    svc = compose["services"][service_name]

    assert f"{volume}:{STATE_DIR}" in svc.get("volumes", []), (
        f"{service_dir}: alert-cooldown state must be on a named volume at {STATE_DIR}"
    )
    assert volume in (compose.get("volumes") or {}), (
        f"{service_dir}: the top-level volumes: block must declare {volume}"
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("service_dir", "wiring"), sorted(DEPLOYMENTS.items()))
def test_cooldown_env_names_are_passed_through(service_dir: str, wiring: tuple[str, str]) -> None:
    """Coolify injects by NAME; a var absent from this list is simply not set in
    the container, and the operator's override silently does nothing."""
    service_name, _ = wiring
    env = _compose(service_dir)["services"][service_name].get("environment", [])
    names = {entry.split("=", 1)[0] for entry in env}

    assert {"ALERT_COOLDOWN_S", "ALERT_STATE_DIR"} <= names, f"{service_dir}: {sorted(names)}"


def test_the_state_dir_is_writable_by_the_runtime_user() -> None:
    """Docker seeds an empty named volume from the image path INCLUDING its
    ownership, so the Dockerfile `chown` is what makes the mount writable. Drop
    it and the container degrades to page-every-tick AND crash-every-tick.

    critical-crons runs as root (it needs /root/.config/rclone at runtime), so
    it needs no chown; critical-canaries runs as `app` and does.
    """
    dockerfile = (CONTAINERS / "critical-canaries" / "Dockerfile").read_text()
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in dockerfile.splitlines()]

    assert any(ln.startswith("RUN ") and STATE_DIR in ln and "chown" in ln for ln in lines), (
        f"critical-canaries Dockerfile must chown {STATE_DIR} to the runtime user"
    )
    # Ordering matters: a chown after USER would run unprivileged and fail.
    chown_at = next(i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if STATE_DIR in ln and "chown" in ln)
    user_at = next(i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.startswith("USER ") and "root" not in ln)
    assert chown_at < user_at, "chown must precede the USER switch"

critical-crons:
    build:
      # Repo root: the Dockerfile copies packages/python and the container tree.
      context: ../../../..
      dockerfile: infra/containers/python/critical-crons/Dockerfile
    # Per-commit tag so previous images remain on the host for rollback.
    # MONOCLOUD_COMMIT is set by the updater; erroring beats an empty tag.
    image: monocloud/critical-crons:${MONOCLOUD_COMMIT:?set by vm-updater}
    container_name: critical-crons-x2ijveyawya9x07cw3eioahw-131232253907
    labels:
      org.opencontainers.image.revision: ${MONOCLOUD_COMMIT:?set by vm-updater}
    command: ['/app/entrypoint.sh']
    env_file:
      # Non-secret config, in git. The host-side secret file is GONE
      # (CIO 2026-09-09) -- see `environment:` below.
      - ./config.critical-crons.env
    # SECRETS, RESOLVED AT APPLY TIME, NEVER STORED ON THIS HOST.
    #
    # Valueless passthroughs: each names a variable and discloses nothing, so
    # this file stays as readable as it was. ETH-mejqj forbids inline VALUES
    # (`- FOO=bar`), which is what leaked ten credentials in one `cat`.
    #
    # The updater resolves these from the vault into its own process env
    # immediately before `compose up` and FAILS CLOSED on any it cannot
    # resolve -- applying with an empty value starts a container that reports
    # healthy while being misconfigured. See dark/vmupdater/stack_secrets.
    environment:
      # EIGHT NAMES BELOW WERE MISSING UNTIL THIS FIX (ETH-vkbuq; first written
      # up 2026-09-22 in PR #1496, which conflicted and never merged). The
      # cutover to vault-at-apply-time dropped names this stack's own
      # critical-crons.env.example declares required, and nothing caught them
      # — because the fail-closed `:?` guard described above only protects
    # as a side effect of this migration.
    mem_limit: 2g
    volumes:

      # gmail-sync container. It is also why cap_drop/no-new-privileges above
      # buy less than they appear to — socket access is root-equivalent on the
      # host. Noted, not solved here.
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - crons-state:/var/lib/monocloud

      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'kill -0 1 2>/dev/null || exit 1']
      interval: 60s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s

import ast
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

_SERVICE_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent
_MAIN_PY = _SERVICE_DIR / "main.py"
_MAIN_SOURCE = _MAIN_PY.read_text()

# Bifrost aliases proven to return empty content for structured extraction.
# Add to this set when a new reasoning alias appears on the gateway; never
# remove one to make a test pass.
REASONING_ALIASES = frozenset({"flash", "glm5"})

_COMPOSE_FILES = (
    _SERVICE_DIR / "docker-compose.yml",
    _SERVICE_DIR / "coolify" / "docker-compose.yaml",
)


def _default_from_compose(path: Path, var: str) -> str:
    """Extract ``${VAR:-default}`` for *var*, whichever compose syntax is used."""
    text = path.read_text()
    m = re.search(rf"{re.escape(var)}[=:]\s*\$\{{{re.escape(var)}:-([^}}]*)\}}", text)
    assert m is not None, f"{path.name} does not set a default for {var}"
    return m.group(1)


def _default_from_source(source: str, var: str) -> str:
    """Extract the literal default from a module-level ``VAR = os.getenv(VAR, lit)``.

    Structural on purpose. If the assignment moves into a function, loses its
    default, or starts computing one, this raises rather than quietly reporting
    a value nothing ships.
    """
    for node in ast.parse(source).body:  # module level only -- not nested scopes
        if not isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
            continue
        if not any(isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == var for t in node.targets):
            continue

        call = node.value
        # `int(os.getenv(...))` and friends wrap the call we want.
        if (
            isinstance(call, ast.Call)
            and isinstance(call.func, ast.Name)
            and call.func.id in {"int", "float", "str"}
            and call.args
        ):
            call = call.args[0]

        assert isinstance(call, ast.Call), f"{var} is not assigned from a call"
        assert isinstance(call.func, ast.Attribute) and call.func.attr == "getenv", (
            f"{var} is not assigned from os.getenv(); this test can no longer "
            "tell what default ships"

# hermes-1 — whole-process containerization

**Status: deployed 2026-08-18 (ETH-r9fi7).** The hermes agent on `hermes-1`
runs inside a container. The four host systemd units are stopped and disabled
but still installed, and are the rollback path.

This directory is the source of truth for that deployment. The parent
[`../README.md`](../README.md) describes the older Coolify-on-zuboff service and
does **not** apply to `hermes-1`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Host | `hermes-1` (Proxmox VM on arendt), reach with `ssh hermes-1` |
| Compose (deployed) | `/opt/hermes-agent/docker-compose.yml` |
| Compose (source) | [`docker-compose.yml`](docker-compose.yml) |
| Image | `hermes-agent:v0.22.2-monocloud11` (`sha256:a0c45ce8…`) running since 2026-10-16 23:11Z (kata ngh4; monocloud10 plus patch 12, headless Bitwarden unlock, deployed together with the Vaultwarden `rawls` login — see [Headless unlock](#headless-unlock-patch-12-kata-ngh4)). Rollback targets, all kept on the host and pinned against `docker-prune` by never-started containers: `hermes-agent:v0.22.2-monocloud10` (`sha256:6dffeb7d…`, pin `hermes-rollback-pin-monocloud10`; compose, `config.yaml` and `.env` as they were in `/root/hermes-ngh4-monocloud11-20261016T230946Z/` — rolling back the image alone leaves `vault.bitwarden.master_password_env` naming a key patch 12 would ignore, which is inert), `hermes-agent:v0.22.2-monocloud9` (`sha256:7d2e0730…`, pin `hermes-rollback-pin-monocloud9`; image-only rollback, no state change), `hermes-agent:v0.22.1-monocloud8` (`sha256:a173d34b…`, pin `hermes-rollback-pin-monocloud8`) and `hermes-agent:c896c09-monocloud5` (`sha256:41fe69ce…`, v0.20.1, pin `hermes-rollback-pin-monocloud5`; see [Rollback](#rollback)). History: `monocloud7` (08:46–09:39Z 2026-10-15) ran with NO `honcho-ai`, see [Runtime dependencies](#runtime-dependencies-pm-generations). Memory config reference: [`docs/infrastructure/HERMES-MEMORY.md`](../../../../../docs/infrastructure/HERMES-MEMORY.md) |
| Container | `hermes` |
| Agent source | upstream NousResearch/hermes-agent tag `v0.22.2` (commit `d923a5eb`), built unmodified as `hermes-agent:v0.22.2` except for the install stamp (see Rebuilding). Upstream: v0.22.1 "was built from the wrong commit"; v0.22.2 is the real release |

## Why
# `crawl4ai` on `research` — cutover runbook

**2026-10-16 (kata ynbs): vm-updater owns this stack.** The live container runs
0.9.5, and its `/srv/crawl4ai` compose service was re-keyed from the Coolify hash
to `crawl4ai`, so the updater's first apply recreates it in place (same project
`crawl4ai`, same service, same `container_name`) instead of colliding with it.
`MANUAL` is gone. Measured before removing it:

- `CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN` and `LLM_API_KEY` (= `BIFROST_VK_CRAWL4AI`) in the live
  container match BWS by SHA-256, and `HOST`, `PORT`, `GUNICORN_BIND`,
  `LLM_BASE_URL` and `LLM_PROVIDER` match `config.crawl4ai.env`.
- The first apply adds what the live stack lacked: `cap_drop: ALL`,
# `searxng` on `research` — cutover runbook

**Nothing here has been executed.** Two things are being fixed at once, and they
are independent of each other.

## 1. The image was unreconstructable

The live stack runs `elqcsvm4ml4ma1i2ow35a3zo:3125ffe3…` — a bare hex repository
name with no registry behind it and no `build:` section. Nothing in that compose
file could rebuild it, so a `docker image prune` would have removed SearXNG

#   - No `coolify` external network and no Traefik labels. Coolify derived
#     routers from labels on the container, so they vanished when it stopped.
#     Ingress here is explicit: the port is published on the TAILNET address and

130 infra/containers/infra/hermes/README.md
# Hermes agent

> **This document describes the older Coolify-on-zuboff `hermes` service and is
> stale for the live deployment.** The hermes agent now runs on the `hermes-1`
> Proxmox VM on arendt, inside a container. See
> [`container/README.md`](container/README.md) for the current deployment,
> runbook, and rollback (ETH-r9fi7, 2026-08-18).

Coolify service `hermes` on zuboff. The operational target is the
`hermes-agent` subservice; `hermes-webui` is the companion UI for inspecting and
controlling the agent. `hermes-agent` exposes its OpenAI-compatible API server
internally on port `8642` so LiteLLM can route and monitor calls as the
`hermes-agent` model alias.

Secrets are sourced from Coolify/BWS. Do not commit values.

| Variable                       | Consumer       | Purpose                                       |
| ------------------------------ | -------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `HERMES_API_SERVER_KEY`        | both           | Bearer key shared by Hermes API and LiteLLM   |
| `DEEPINFRA_API_KEY`            | `hermes-agent` | DeepInfra provider access for the agent model |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`           | `hermes-agent` | OpenRouter fallback/provider access           |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`            | `hermes-agent` | Anthropic provider access                     |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY`               | `hermes-agent` | OpenAI provider access                        |
| `SERVICE_PASSWORD_HERMESWEBUI` | `hermes-webui` | Web UI password                               |

## LiteLLM routing

LiteLLM exposes this agent as `hermes-agent`. The existing LiteLLM `hermes` alias
remains a DeepInfra-hosted Nous-Hermes model and must not be replaced by the
agent route.

Coolify deploys Hermes and LiteLLM as separate resources. By default, each stack
uses its own UUID-named Docker network, so cross-stack DNS requires Coolify's
**Connect to Predefined Network** behavior. When enabled, Coolify may require the
generated service/container hostname rather than the short compose service name.
The current zuboff default for LiteLLM is:

```text
HERMES_AGENT_API_BASE=http://REDACTED:8642/v1
```

Do not add a public `SERVICE_FQDN`/Traefik route for the Hermes API server unless
that is explicitly approved; the API server has agent tooling behind it.

## Active Hermes profile

The live gateway reads model/provider state from the persisted Hermes home volume,
not only from container process env. During the 2026-06-03 rollout, the active
root config (`/home/hermes/.hermes/config.yaml`) and named profiles were patched
to:

```yaml
model:
  default: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
  provider: custom:deepinfra

custom_providers:
  - name: deepinfra
    base_url: https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai
    key_env: DEEPINFRA_API_KEY
    model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
```

The persisted `/home/hermes/.hermes/.env` must contain:

```text
API_SERVER_ENABLED=true
API_SERVER_HOST=0.0.0.0
API_SERVER_PORT=8642
API_SERVER_MODEL_NAME=hermes-agent
API_SERVER_KEY=<from HERMES_API_SERVER_KEY>
DEEPINFRA_API_KEY=REDACTED BWS>
```

Why this matters: container env updates alone were visible to `docker exec` but
not to the long-running gateway's provider/API-server config. After changing
Coolify env, either redeploy through a path that refreshes the persisted Hermes
home config or update `/home/hermes/.hermes/.env` intentionally and restart
`hermes-agent`.

## Operations

```bash
coolify service get ov9dl733u21x9ze20ovh1flp --context zuboff-public --format json
coolify service restart ov9dl733u21x9ze20ovh1flp --context zuboff-public
```

Use Coolify for logs/runtime inspection; this repo stores the desired source
configuration and service inventory only.

content.content:
# critical-canaries

Host-independent freshness pager. Runs on **zuboff** under Coolify (supercronic,
every 15 min). Replaces the noisy full `infra-health` sweep, which was disabled
on rawls on 2026-07-12 (ETH-ur07qv) because it paged constantly and — being
rawls-resident — would die silently when rawls is decommissioned.

## What it watches

Only three high-consequence tripwires (freshness of these `catalog.pipeline_runs`
freshness row. See `docs/adr/2026-07-12-critical-canaries-zuboff-keeper.md`.

## Environment (injected by Coolify from BWS, by name)

- `SUPABASE_DB_URL` — reads `catalog.pipeline_runs`; `PipelineRun` upserts to it
- `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` — alert delivery
- `POSTHOG_API_KEY`, `POSTHOG_HOST` — optional; `PipelineRun` degrades gracefully
- `GARAGE_METRICS_URL` — optional; enables the Garage block canary (Probe A).
  e.g. `http://garage:3903/metrics` on the Coolify network
- `GARAGE_METRICS_TOKEN` — optional; BWS `GARAGE_ZUBOFF_METRICS_TOKEN`
- `GARAGE_STATS_CMD` — optional; Probe B fallback (e.g. `docker exec <garage> /garage stats`)
- `GARAGE_RESYNC_ERROR_MAX`, `GARAGE_RESYNC_QUEUE_MAX` — optional thresholds
  (defaults `10` / `100`; see `dark.health.canary.garage`)
- `GARAGE_S3_INTERNAL_ENDPOINT`, `GARAGE_FORGEJO_ACCESS_KEY`,
  `GARAGE_FORGEJO_SECRET_KEY` — **all three required** to enable the forgejo
  backup-freshness check (ETH-hxdrr). The endpoint is the garage container's
  **S3 API** on the shared `coolify` network (`:3900` — not the `:3903`
  metrics port). `GARAGE_FORGEJO_*` is RWO on `monocloud-forgejo` only.
- `FORGEJO_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_S`, `FORGEJO_BACKUP_MIN_BYTES`,
  `FORGEJO_BACKUP_BUCKET`, `FORGEJO_BACKUP_PREFIX` — optional; defaults
  `93600` (26h), `1000000`, `monocloud-forgejo`, `postgres/`
`Up` for 31 minutes holding entirely empty credentials.

If any of the three required vars is unset the check is skipped silently, the
same convention the Garage probe uses. **Adding the code is not enough — the
vars must be set on the Coolify app or this canary is inert.**

### Vault backup freshness (kata xb6h)

(`ZFS_POOL_WARN_PCT=40`) for a `run()`-level check.

## Where this actually runs (2026-08-24)

**arendt `prod` VM, managed by the pull-based vm-updater (ETH-bfk84) — not
Coolify, not zuboff, and no longer hand-deployed.** The updater builds the
image ON the VM from the checkout; the image never enters any registry
(Sloane, 2026-08-24 — keep the canaries image out of registries).

| | |
|---|---|
| stack | [`infra/stacks/prod/critical-canaries/docker-compose.yaml`](../../../stacks/prod/critical-canaries/docker-compose.yaml) — the ONE definition; the updater reconciles it every 10 min. The old hand-managed `/srv/critical-canaries/` copy and the committed `deploy/docker-compose.prod.yaml` are retired (two definitions of one stack is the drift ETH-b2hbe punished). |
| env | `/etc/monocloud/critical-canaries.env`, `0600 root` — **not** in git, values from BWS |
| state volume | `critical-canaries-state` — the alert-state was **copied** out of Coolify's `u34dvj85i38lvahvgtn87lwu_critical-canaries-state` before the app was deleted; that original is now removed |

The volume is deliberately the **same one Coolify created**. A fresh volume resets
the alert cooldown and restores the 96-pages-a-day flood ETH-y2ve7 fixed, and it
would do so silently.

**`GARAGE_S3_INTERNAL_ENDPOINT` is host-specific and the BWS value is wrong here.**
BWS holds the zuboff docker-network name (`http://garage-<uuid>:3900`), which does
not resolve from arendt. Garage moved to the arendt `garage` CT (re-measured
2026-10-09: tailnet IP `100.120.121.110`, MagicDNS `garage.worm-chimera.ts.net`,
live health on `:3903`). The canary runs in a bridge-networked container, which
cannot resolve MagicDNS names (ETH-21vkp) — so set the tailnet IP:
`http://100.120.121.110:3900`, with `GARAGE_METRICS_URL` on the same host at
`:3903`. Copying the BWS value onto an arendt host yields a permanently BLIND
canary that nonetheless looks configured.

**The Coolify apps are deleted (2026-08-18).** Both of them —
`demvmgdy50g9tme6ieitai62` (zuboff) and `u34dvj85i38lvahvgtn87lwu` (arendt
prod-vm) — and `critical-canaries` is out of `scripts/ci/coolify-deploy-map.json`,
so CI cannot trigger a redeploy. This was not theoretical tidying: **both were
running at once**, paging the same Telegram channel with separate cooldown
state, so a firing incident could alert twice and neither instance could resolve
the other's.

The image, the state volume, and the alert state now live outside Coolify's
naming namespace, so nothing Coolify does can reclaim them. Deleting the app
*did* remove the local retag once — the image survived only because Coolify's
own tag still pointed at the same ID. There is now a
`docker save` tarball at `/srv/critical-canaries/images/` as the backstop.
The image has **no registry behind it**: do not `docker compose pull`. Rebuild
from `infra/containers/python/critical-canaries/Dockerfile` at the repo root.

### Verifying a canary is live

A green tick is not evidence. `0 garage/backup/forgejo breach line(s)` is
byte-identical whether the check ran and passed or was skipped for missing
config. Prove it fires, in isolation so nothing pages and the real cooldown
state is untouched:

```bash
# backup canary
docker run --rm --env-file /etc/monocloud/critical-canaries.env \
  -e FORGEJO_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_S=1 -e ALERT_STATE_DIR=/tmp/probe \
  -e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN= REDACTED TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID= \
  --entrypoint /app/.venv/bin/python <image> /app/src/main.py

# liveness canary — point it at a dead port; expect an UNREACHABLE breach line
docker run --rm --env-file /etc/monocloud/critical-canaries.env \
  -e FORGEJO_HEALTH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9/api/healthz -e ALERT_STATE_DIR=/tmp/probe \
  -e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN= REDACTED TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID= \
  --entrypoint /app/.venv/bin/python <image> /app/src/main.py
```

Expect `1 garage/backup/forgejo breach line(s)` from each; the real config gives
`0`. Point `GARAGE_S3_INTERNAL_ENDPOINT` at `http://127.0.0.1:9` for the backup
BLIND path. Note the entrypoint must be `/app/.venv/bin/python` — the system
`python3` has no `psycopg2`.

## Deploy (Coolify on zuboff)

Git-source `dockercompose` Application. **CI-wired**: `deploy.yml`'s
`deploy-coolify` job triggers the Coolify API on every push to `dev`, routed by
the explicit map in `scripts/ci/coolify-deploy-map.json` — not by the
`deploy:coolify` tag. Git-watch webhooks never fire here because
`coolify.ec1c.com` sits behind CF Access (ETH-zq5wh).

**First deploy after a cooldown change is clean** — the named volume starts
empty, so the gate sees no prior state and behaves as a first observation. It
does not emit a spurious all-clear.

No FQDN / Traefik route (headless cron) — do not PATCH `docker_compose_domains`.

## Local test

```bash
npx nx test critical-canaries      # pure-function filter tests, no DB
npx nx lint critical-canaries      # ruff + mypy
```

cannot resolve MagicDNS names (ETH-21vkp) — so set the tailnet IP:

A green tick is not evidence. `0 garage/backup/forgejo breach line(s)` is
byte-identical whether the check ran and passed or was skipped for missing
config. Prove it fires, in isolation so nothing pages and the real cooldown
state is untouched:

  -e FORGEJO_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_S=1 -e ALERT_STATE_DIR=/tmp/probe \

Git-source `dockercompose` Application. **CI-wired**: `deploy.yml`'s

the explicit map in `scripts/ci/coolify-deploy-map.json` — not by the
`deploy:coolify` tag. Git-watch webhooks never fire here because
`coolify.ec1c.com` sits behind CF Access (ETH-zq5wh).

**First deploy after a cooldown change is clean** — the named volume starts
empty, so the gate sees no prior state and behaves as a first observation. It
does not emit a spurious all-clear.

No FQDN / Traefik route (headless cron) — do not PATCH `docker_compose_domains`.

```bash

Credentials are ``GARAGE_FORGEJO_*`` (RWO on ``monocloud-forgejo`` only); the

age-encrypted ``vault-<stamp>.tar.gz.age`` to ``monocloud-vault/vaultwarden/``
the docs described as live was watching nothing. Deploy freshness of THIS
container is therefore load-bearing.

Two of them were later found running AT ONCE (zuboff + arendt), paging the same
Telegram chat with separate cooldown state, which is why the Coolify apps were
deleted rather than merely stopped: this keeper's resolve/cooldown machinery
assumes one writer per service key.

# ALERT_STATE_DIR must point at a Docker volume, NOT the default under $HOME:
# this container is recreated on every Coolify deploy, and container-local state
# would silently reset the cooldown and restore the flood.
SERVICE = "critical-canaries"

# missing => ImportError, both follower crons down.
COPY scripts/ci/follower_cascade_fk.py ./scripts/ci/follower_cascade_fk.py
COPY scripts/ci/follower_auth_refs.py ./scripts/ci/follower_auth_refs.py

# canary above: the follower is reachable only from inside the coolify network.
# Its logic lives in dark.health.follower_parity, already present via the

test on ops shows the `docker` CLI in this container can't reach the
daemon under that hardening, relax `cap_drop` first and re-test — don't
touch anything else in the compose file to work around it.

The container name is still Coolify-hashed (e.g. `gmail-sync-<hash>-1`) —
inherited from the zuboff deployment and never renamed —
not the rawls default `email-gmail-sync`, so the crontab resolves it by name
prefix at cron time:

```
docker ps --filter name=gmail-sync --format '{{.Names}}' | head -n1
```

## Environment (injected by Coolify from BWS, by name)

- `SUPABASE_DB_URL` — all four pipelines read/write `catalog.pipeline_runs`; the DR backup dumps this DB; the gmail-gap and zernio pipelines also query/write `comms.gmail_messages` / `catalog.social_*` directly.
- `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` — alert delivery (`dark.notify`).
- `POSTHOG_API_KEY`, `POSTHOG_HOST` — optional; `PipelineRun` degrades gracefully without them.
- `R2_LAKE_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_LAKE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `R2_LAKE_ENDPOINT` — `dark.storage.create_r2_client()` for the reconciler **and** the DR backup's `r2:` remote (writes to `r2:lake/backups/supabase/`).
- `HETZNER_STORAGE_BOX_URL`, `HETZNER_STORAGE_BOX_USER`, `HETZNER_STORAGE_BOX_PASSWORD` — the DR backup's `sbox:` remote (Hetzner Storagebox over SFTP). Password is obscured by `entrypoint.sh` before it reaches rclone's config.
- `AGENTIC_INBOX_IMPORT_SECRET`, `SEND_APPROVAL_SECRET` — reconciler replay auth against the inbox worker.
- `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID`, `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET` — CF Access service token for `inbox.ec1c.com`.
- `INBOX_URL` (default `https://inbox.ec1c.com`), `INBOX_MAILBOX_ID` (has a script-level default) — reconciler replay target.
- `ZERNIO_API_KEY` — Zernio API bearer token for the social sync.

The DR backup also needs the `age` **public** key to encrypt — that key is a
literal in `supabase_pg_backup.py` (public by design; the private key stays
offline for restore), so no env var is required for it.

```bash
npx nx test critical-crons      # structural tests, no DB/network/docker
npx nx lint critical-crons      # ruff + mypy
npx nx build critical-crons     # docker build (linux/amd64) — the real gate
```

Note: this project has no installable Python package of its own — the
pipeline scripts live in `data-pipelines/backup`, `data-pipelines/comms`, and
`data-pipelines/social` (copied into the image, invoked by absolute path from
the crontab) and all business logic comes from the `dark-core` path
dependency. `lint` and `mypy` therefore only run against `tests/`, not a
`src/` directory (there isn't one) — see the `pyproject.toml` comment on

**This container has NO working deploy command.** It was a Coolify Git-source
application on **zuboff**; zuboff was cancelled at the ETH-ceqf9 cutover and

`docker compose` stack at `/srv/critical-crons` on the **ops** LXC — the
container name still carries the old Coolify app UUID, which is the only trace
of that history.

1. **`packages/python` is baked in at build time** (`Dockerfile`,
   `COPY packages/python /packages/python`). Merging a fix to the shared
   package does NOT reach these crons. The image must be rebuilt.
# still uploading.
45 5 * * * flock -n -E 75 /tmp/supabase_pg_backup.lock /app/.venv/bin/python /app/scripts/cron/cron_heartbeat_wrapper.py --pipeline supabase_backup_prune -- /app/.venv/bin/python /app/data-pipelines/backup/supabase_backup_prune.py

# container name is Coolify-hashed on zuboff (not the rawls default

*/30 * * * * /app/.venv/bin/python /app/scripts/cron/cron_heartbeat_wrapper.py --pipeline gmail_gap_check -- /app/.venv/bin/python /app/data-pipelines/comms/gmail_gap_autobackfill.py --container "$(docker ps --filter name=gmail-sync --format '{{.Names}}' | head -n1)"

# onto the zuboff DR follower; this finds versions present on prod but missing
# on the follower and invokes scripts/ci/apply-follower-migrations.sh.
# Lives HERE, not in Forgejo Actions: the follower binds 127.0.0.1:5433 on the
# zuboff host (NOT a public ingress), so a CI runner has no route to it. In the
# coolify docker network it is pg-follower:5432 (PG_FOLLOWER_HOST/PORT in the
# compose). Paging is via the critical-canaries KEEPERS entry on this
# pipeline's heartbeat, not a CI job.
*/15 * * * * /app/.venv/bin/python /app/scripts/cron/cron_heartbeat_wrapper.py --pipeline follower_migration_replay_canary -- /app/.venv/bin/python /app/scripts/cron/follower_migration_replay_canary.py

def follower_env(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """A prod DSN present, follower credentials absent — the observed prod shape.

    `PG_FOLLOWER_PASSWORD` is declared bare in the critical-crons compose, so an
    unset Coolify value arrives as an EMPTY string rather than an absent one.
    `delenv` and an empty value take the same branch in `_follower_dsn()`, which
    is the case being pinned.
    """

# Email Sync Migration History

## 2026-05-13 — rawls → Coolify on zuboff (current)

**From**: rawls Docker Compose
**To**: Coolify Application on zuboff
**Status**: COMPLETE
**Tickets**: ETH-1498 (gmail), ETH-1499 (admin-reports), ETH-1500 (calendar), ETH-1502 (contacts)
**Handoff**: `docs/handoffs/2026-05-13-rawls-decom-coolify-cutover.md` (removed 2026-10-14; in git history)

All 4 daemon services deployed as a single Coolify Application from git
(`infra/containers/python/email/coolify/docker-compose.yaml`). App UUID
`bt5vpelbgxqq7dwxzgrltpqg`, project `ka16no6pm6a9w6x1hqkfc0cj`.

Storage switched from R2 `lake` to garage S3 `monocloud-email-sync`:

- R2 returned 403/AccessDenied from zuboff IPs with the same credentials
  that worked from rawls. Suspected R2 token IP-scoping.
- Garage avoids cross-cloud round-trip and isolates email-sync output
  from the R2-mirror `lake` bucket.
- BWS keys: `GARAGE_EMAIL_SYNC_ACCESS_KEY_ID`,
  `GARAGE_EMAIL_SYNC_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.
- Endpoint: was `GARAGE_ZUBOFF_S3_ENDPOINT` (`https://s3.zuboff.ec1c.com`, dead
  with zuboff; key retired). Consumers now use `GARAGE_S3_INTERNAL_ENDPOINT` —
  the arendt `garage` CT over the tailnet (ETH-mx17v).

Code changes that landed with the migration:

- `dark.storage.create_r2_client` now defaults to path-style
  addressing. R2 supports both; garage requires path-style.
- `gmail_sync._save_to_r2` HeadObject idempotency check tolerates
  HTTP 400 the same as 404. Garage returns 400 on HEAD for missing
  keys; the old check raised, killing the message.

Rawls containers stopped 2026-05-13 00:04Z. Images + state volumes
retained 48h for rollback (named volumes `email_{gmail,calendar,contacts,admin-reports}-state`).

State files re-derived on first Coolify run — Google sync tokens
refresh naturally; admin-reports is now retired because `catalog.webhooks`
was dropped on 2026-06-11 after unbounded payload storage caused production
database bloat.

---

## 2025-10-06 — workers/ingest → infra/containers/python/email on rawls

**From**: workers/ingest (Cloudflare Workers scheduled cron)
**To**: infra/containers/python/email (Docker on rawls)

**Date**: 2025-10-06
**Status**: COMPLETE (then migrated again 2026-05-13 — see above)

---

## Why Migrate?

**Workers limitations** (workers/ingest):

- ❌ CPU time: 30s per invocation (scheduled), max 15min (workflows)
- ❌ Subrequest limit: 50 per invocation
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Manual redeploy of contacts-sync on the arendt `comms` CT (111). ETH-bi8ow.
#
# THIS IS A MANUAL DEPLOY. Nothing runs it automatically: Coolify, which used
# to build these containers, was deleted on 2026-08-21, and the email stack
# on comms has no vm-updater stack or systemd unit. A merge to `dev` does NOT
# reach this container. Run this script by hand from a monocloud checkout.
#
# How the container gets its config
#   The compose project is `mail-sync`, file /srv/mail-sync/docker-compose.yaml
#   on comms. That file is Coolify's rendered output: it holds the
#   contacts-sync `environment:` block as inline literals and also loads
#   /srv/mail-sync/.env via `env_file`. Both files hold secrets and neither is
#   in git. Do not read or print them. This script edits exactly one
#   non-secret line of the compose file, the contacts-sync `image:` line.
#   It does not touch the env, networks, the volume

This container used to poll Google Admin Reports and POST every audit event to
``catalog.webhooks``. That table was intentionally retired because it had become
an unbounded event-log sink. The compose/Coolify service definitions were also
removed with the catalog.webhooks drop migration.

Keep this file as a fail-closed compatibility shim for stale images or manual
  / `_upsert_event`). Requires SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY; degrades
  to R2-only (with a startup warning) when either is unset.
- Also publishes to a legacy queue webhook (QUEUE_WEBHOOK_URL) for
  processing into Cloudflare D1. That queue pipeline has been dormant since
  Feb 2026 (Coolify retired 2026-08-21; COOLIFY-ENV-MAP.md removed) and the Coolify
  calendar-sync service has never had QUEUE_WEBHOOK_URL/QUEUE_API_TOKEN set
  — this call is a no-op today and D1's `calendar_events` table is a
  different datastore from Supabase `comms.calendar_events` regardless.

ETH-56l8ta (2026-08-03): audit found `comms.calendar_events` had 6279 rows
but nothing in this file ever wrote to Supabase — the container's Coolify
compose entry lacked SUPABASE_URL/SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY entirely (unlike its
gmail-sync/contacts-sync siblings), and the code had no upsert path even if
the env had been set. The existing rows were frozen at 2026-02-22 (last
`updated_at`), meaning ~5+ months of calendar events were never landing in

# Research Queue Worker

Coolify-owned research services for zuboff.

This replaces the legacy rawls cron/systemd queue worker and the manual
defeatbeta volume seed. The Coolify Application does not expose HTTP.

Services:

- `research-queue-worker`: persistent daemon polling `research.pipeline_jobs`

The pipeline expects the Yahoo parquet cache at `/srv/data/defeatbeta/data/`:

- `stock_earning_call_transcripts.parquet`
- `stock_news.parquet`
- `stock_statement.parquet`

The Coolify compose mounts a named volume at `/srv/data/defeatbeta`. The
`defeatbeta-sync` sidecar seeds it on startup:

```bash
(currently `rawls`) unless `ALLOW_QUEUE_WORKER_ON_BLOCKED_HOST=1` is set for
an explicit emergency bypass.

## Deployment

Coolify app `research-queue` (`y4xdlvh2oiq408ddgz6v92dd`) is configured as a
git-sourced dockercompose app on branch `dev`, with base directory
`/containers/python/research-queue/coolify`.

The Coolify app UUID is listed in `scripts/ci/coolify-deploy-map.json`'s
`deploys` set, so Forgejo's `deploy-coolify` job (`.forgejo/workflows/deploy.yml`)
triggers a Coolify deploy on affected `dev` pushes. It uses the Coolify deploy
endpoint, not restart, so code changes rebuild the image before the worker
container restarts.

## LiteLLM Routing

**There is no app-specific override any more.** LiteLLM left zuboff for the
arendt `prod` VM on 2026-08-18 (ETH-ox6my.3), so the Coolify docker network
(`sph12w5e5ptqg7yiai6mmjf4`) and the `http://litellm:4000` name inside it are
both gone, as is the Cloudflare Access route at `litellm.ec1c.com`.

The worker now uses the **global BWS** `LITELLM_BASE_URL` — the tailnet URL that
`dark.llm.get_litellm_config()` resolves for every caller in the repo. One
value, one place to change it.

This README previously said "do not put that internal Docker URL in global BWS",
which was correct advice for a docker-network-local name and is exactly why the
override existed. That reasoning no longer applies: the gateway is reachable at
one address from everywhere on the tailnet, so a per-app override would only be
a second place for the URL to go stale.

## Migration Flags & Rollback Controls

The research pipeline phase is recorded as `dual` (ETH-wl79m, 2026-09-30), a
stale label since kata x2cx (2026-10-14): every note save writes the structured
document (`research.save_note_structured`) ONLY. Nothing in the pipeline writes
the legacy `research.companies.research_note_body`, and no flag gates the
structured write. The flags do less than their names suggest:

- `STRUCTURED_CANONICAL_WRITE_ENABLED` (deployed `true`, code default `false`):
  labels the aggregate sync pass and makes `sync_research_to_db.py` refuse
  `--source=markdown`. It does **not** turn structured writes on or off.
- `MARKDOWN_EXPORT_WRITEBACK_ENABLED` (deployed `true`, code default `true`):
  runs the aggregate pass after completed jobs (tick reconcile only; the
  DB -> markdown compat export is retired, kata x2cx). `false` skips it;
  per-job DB writes are unaffected.
- `LEGACY_MARKDOWN_CANONICAL_READ_FALLBACK`: **no code reader** since PR #303
  (ETH-7hpo8c); it survives only in the CI phase policy.

Deployed values: `infra/stacks/research/research-workers/config.research-queue-worker.env`.
Rollback (vm-updater, and why a flag rollback cannot stop structured writes):
`docs/infrastructure/dapr-bridge-runbook.md`, "Rollback: `dual` -> `legacy`".
The daily body-vs-sections parity canary was retired with the body write
(kata x53t).

## Cutover Checklist

1. Seed `/srv/data/defeatbeta` in the Coolify volume and verify the healthcheck
   turns healthy. The `defeatbeta-sync` sidecar should do this automatically on
   first start.
2. Disable any live rawls `pipeline-queue` cron entry and systemd service before
   starting the Coolify daemon.
3. Sync required env vars into the Coolify Application by name from BWS; never
   paste values into documentation or logs.
4. Start the daemon and verify it claims only pending jobs from
   `research.pipeline_jobs`.
# defeatbeta parquet sync — refresh local Yahoo Finance cache for research.
# Times are UTC. The entrypoint also runs this once at container startup so a
# fresh Coolify volume becomes usable without waiting for the next schedule.
# Wrapped so a non-zero exit (incl. 75, lock timeout) records last_status=failed
# for sync_yahoo_data; the script's own PipelineRun writes the success heartbeat.

# Containers

> **⚠ zuboff is OFFLINE (verified 2026-08-22) and Coolify is gone with it.**
> The services in the zuboff table below now run as hand-managed docker on
> arendt CTs: email stack (email-triage-agent, email-archiver, triage-scorer,
> gmail/calendar/contacts-sync) on `comms` under `/srv/<svc>/`; crawl4ai and
> searxng on `research` under `/srv/` (the inbox-core/rawls Dapr stack there was
> retired 2026-10-01 (ETH-ycgxw.2); research workers there
> are a vm-updater tenant since 2026-09-13, `infra/stacks/research/`); pg-follower on the `pgdr` VM (host postgres); qdrant + litellm
> (soak-only) + bifrost (the LLM gateway) + critical-canaries on the `prod`
> VM. Deploy = edit `/srv/<svc>/docker-compose.yaml` + `docker compose up -d`
> on the CT; bridge containers must use tailnet IPs, not `*.ts.net` names
> (ETH-21vkp). The tables below predate the move and are retained as
> reference until the consolidation docs land (ETH-ceqf9 / A4).

Docker services formerly deployed on **zuboff (Coolify)**. **Railway is fully decommissioned (2026-07-31, ETH-apd5w)** — no live Railway services remain; the `deploy:railway` tag and the `deploy-railway` CI job were removed. **rawls is fully decommissioned (2026-07-31, ETH-ysv5xq)** — the rawls table below is retained as historical/last-known-state only; the post-decommission disposition of every service it listed was verified and closed out in ETH-9mtc8 (2026-08-18). See [`docs/CI-DEPLOY.md`](../docs/CI-DEPLOY.md) for full deploy pipeline. Full server inventory: [`docs/infrastructure/SERVERS.md`](../docs/infrastructure/SERVERS.md).

Follow the hand-authored [Dark agent charter](../AGENTS.md); this file adds
component guidance. Do not regenerate root `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` from
inherited templates. Edit manifest-owned agent sources only for their declared
distribution targets, as described in `infra/devices/agents/` at the repo root.

**Migration direction**: zuboff and Coolify are both GONE (Coolify deleted 2026-08-21, zuboff permanently down). New services target arendt VMs with raw Docker; container deploys are currently UNAUTOMATED (ETH-ms976). The `coolify-deploy` skill and the `COOLIFY-*.md` reference docs were deleted 2026-09-02 — do not look for them, and do not propose a Coolify deploy. Where each container lands is still open.

## zuboff (Coolify — RETIRED 2026-08-21)

> **Historical.** Coolify's control plane was deleted 2026-08-21 and zuboff is
> permanently down. Nothing below deploys any more; the `git-watch auto-deploy`
> claim was never true even then (ETH-zq5wh). The `containers/*/coolify/`
> compose files are RETAINED deliberately — they are the surviving record of
> each service's env, volumes and labels, and are the source material for
> re-homing onto arendt. Read them as configuration history, not as a deploy path.

Compose lives at `containers/<service>/coolify/docker-compose.yaml` (or `infra/containers/ts/<service>/coolify/...`).

| Service | Purpose | Cutover |
|---|---|---|
| `qdrant` | Vector DB (`research_notes`, `filing_chunks`, `transcript_chunks`, etc.) | 2026-05-13 |
| `litellm` + `litellm-db` | AI gateway proxy + paired Postgres | 2026-05-13 |
| `email-triage-agent` (`infra/containers/ts/email-triage/coolify/`) | PII-redact + LLM-classify unscored emails to `hitl.review_queue` or `comms.email_ai_scores` | 2026-05-21 (ETH-1724) |
| `email-sync` (`infra/containers/python/email/coolify/`, app `bt5vpelbgxqq7dwxzgrltpqg`): gmail-sync, calendar-sync, contacts-sync, admin-reports-sync | Gmail/Calendar/Contacts sync to R2 + Supabase | 2026-05-13 |
| `research-queue-worker`, `defeatbeta-sync` | Research pipeline workers | — |
| `pg-follower-monocloud` | Logical-replication follower of Supabase prod (ETH-1562) | — |
| `forgejo` + db | Self-hosted git eval | — |
| `kener` + redis | Public status page (status.ethicic.com) | — |
| ~~`garage`~~ | Self-hosted S3 — **moved to the arendt `garage` CT 107 as a native `garage.service`** (config captured at `infra/hosts/garage/etc/garage.toml`, ETH-mx17v); not a container any more | — |
| ~~`inbox-core`~~ + ~~`inbox-agent`~~ (ex `rawls-core`/`rawls-agent`, ETH-lywjz) | Dapr dispatch gateway + agent runtime + Redis | **RETIRED 2026-10-01 (ETH-ycgxw.2)** — stopped on the research CT 2026-09-15; inbox dispatch goes to Hermes (ETH-emux1). `containers/ts/inbox-core` and `containers/python/inbox-agent` deleted from the tree (ETH-ox6my.9). |
| `crawl4ai` | JS-rendered page scraping (app `xsj8fga8m6lla6tqo1qzakn9`) | confirmed running, ETH-jzigx (2026-07-23) |
| `searxng` | Self-hosted metasearch (app `elqcsvm4ml4ma1i2ow35a3zo`) | confirmed running, ETH-jzigx (2026-07-23) |
| `triage-scorer` (`infra/containers/ts/triage-scorer`, app `ko9ykqezvwre61dd37pz6nbh`) | Daily scoring job for unified triage action queue | confirmed running, ETH-jzigx (2026-07-23) — **app's configured source path is stale** (`/services/triage-scorer`, not the current `infra/containers/ts/triage-scorer` layout); needs operator reconciliation |
| `email-archiver` (`infra/containers/ts/email-archiver`, app `r75xzy9crye7d3twfw72z0w1`) | Cron job: auto-archive low-value scored emails (never deletes) | confirmed running, ETH-jzigx (2026-07-23) — still on the pre-`/coolify/` compose layout |
| ~~`vector`~~ | Log aggregation — **moved to the arendt `vector` CT 108 as a native `vector.service`** 2026-08-19; running config captured at `infra/hosts/vector/etc/vector/vector.toml` | `containers/infra/vector/coolify/` (app `n2nf41kkc72offqcr14op1lo`) deleted 2026-09-05 (ETH-mx17v) — the one exception to "compose files are retained" above, because the captured native config supersedes it; only `project.json` + the shape test remain |

## rawls (DECOMMISSIONED 2026-07-31 — no rawls containers remain as of ETH-9mtc8, 2026-08-18)

`ssh rawls` no longer resolves; the host is gone. Prior to decommission, deploy was via CI: SSH + rsync + docker-compose, services in `containers/` or `infra/containers/ts/`. ETH-9mtc8 (2026-08-18) verified the disposition of the last four `deploy:docker` stragglers — `video-processing`, `web-monitor`, `verifications-consumer`, `rspamd` — against the 2026-08-14 container audit (`docs/infrastructure/2026-08-14-container-audit-zuboff-focault.md`): none exists on zuboff or focault, none was migrated, and all four project directories were deleted from the tree. The `deploy:docker` tag is retired repo-wide. The row below is the only rawls-era entry that survives (it went on to zuboff Coolify, then native on arendt).

| Directory | Service | Last-known purpose | Last-known disposition (pre-decommission) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `containers/` | vector | Log aggregation (JSON POSTs → object archive + PostHog material route) | Was dual-deployed (rawls-local + zuboff Coolify, app `n2nf41kkc72offqcr14op1lo`). Both halves are gone: it now runs **natively on the arendt `vector` CT** (`vector.service`; captured at `infra/hosts/vector/etc/vector/vector.toml`), and `containers/infra/vector/coolify/` was deleted 2026-09-05 (ETH-mx17v). |

**Deleted 2026-08-18 (ETH-9mtc8, gone with rawls — not migrated):** `video-processing` (transcript extraction; stopped/crashlooping since 2026-05-21), `web-monitor` (exclusion watchdog; ETH-1443 Coolify plan never executed), `verifications-consumer` (pgmq `verifications` consumer, ETH-1018), `rspamd` (mail filtering; already absent from rawls `docker ps` on 2026-07-23). `email-triage`'s optional `RSPAMD_URL` integration stays in code, disabled by default. Their data-layer leftovers (roles, pgmq queue, Garage bucket) are tracked in ETH-jrrdm.

**Retired from this directory** (moved to zuboff section above): `qdrant`, `litellm`, `email-triage-agent`, `email-sync` (rsync-to-rawls `deploy` target removed in ETH-nkkj0; the local dev `docker-compose.yml`/`up`/`down`/`logs` targets in `infra/containers/python/email/project.json` remain for developer use), `rawls-core` (retired 2026-10-01, ETH-ycgxw.2), `crawl4ai`, `searxng`, `triage-scorer`, `email-archiver` (ETH-jzigx, 2026-07-23 — confirmed live Coolify apps; their Nx `deploy` targets, where present, still run the legacy rawls rsync/SSH command and need a follow-up to point at `coolify deploy uuid ...` instead).

## Railway (DECOMMISSIONED 2026-07-31 — no live services)

Railway is fully retired (ETH-apd5w). It previously hosted `archivebox` (web
archiving) and `mcp-server`; both are gone from the deploy pipeline. `archivebox`
was removed from the tree entirely (the `archivebox/` R2 archive data is
retained); `mcp-server` was removed from the tree on 2026-08-18 (ETH-lywjz) —
it had been reduced to a README + Railway-only `project.json`. `crawl4ai` and `searxng`
run on zuboff/Coolify (see the zuboff table above) — the `RAILWAY_CRAWL4AI_*` /
`RAILWAY_SEARXNG_URL` BWS names are legacy misnomers, not a Railway dependency.

## Shared code

Shared Python domains live in `packages/python/dark/` (repo root), imported as
`dark.<domain>`, not under `containers/`. `containers/python-shared/` does not exist. See `packages/python/CLAUDE.md`.

## Conventions

- Secrets: BWS (project: `monocloud`). See root CLAUDE.md.
- Each container has its own `pyproject.toml`, `.venv`, and Nx `project.json`.
- Python targets: `install` (uv sync), `test` (pytest), `lint` (ruff + mypy). Test/lint depend on install.
- Custom images embed the BWS CLI and invoke the container with `bws run --`.
- **(Retired 2026-08-21, Coolify deleted)** Former Coolify Application compose path: `containers/<svc>/coolify/docker-compose.yaml` — Coolify pulls from the watched branch (`dev`), env vars wired via `coolify app env create/update` (not committed). Any lingering rawls-side `docker-compose.yml` files are now dead weight (rawls decommissioned 2026-07-31) — safe to delete once confirmed unused, no transition period left to preserve.
- **Bumping a Python container's interpreter version**: the Dockerfile's `FROM python:...` tag must exact-match the project's `.python-version`, or `uv sync` silently downloads its own managed interpreter as root and the non-root runtime user can't read it (this took down `research-queue` in prod — ETH-od5s9). Procedure + verification checklist: [`../docs/development/PYTHON-VERSION-BUMPS.md`](../docs/development/PYTHON-VERSION-BUMPS.md). If you're bumping the same container's version repeatedly, also read [`../docs/development/RUST-MIGRATION-SIGNALS.md`](../docs/development/RUST-MIGRATION-SIGNALS.md).

- Each container has its own `pyproject.toml`, `.venv`, and Nx `project.json`.
- Python targets: `install` (uv sync), `test` (pytest), `lint` (ruff + mypy). Test/lint depend on install.
- Custom images embed the BWS CLI and invoke the container with `bws run --`.
- **(Retired 2026-08-21, Coolify deleted)** Former Coolify Application compose path: `containers/<svc>/coolify/docker-compose.yaml` — Coolify pulls from the watched branch (`dev`), env vars wired via `coolify app env create/update` (not committed). Any lingering rawls-side `docker-compose.yml` files are now dead weight (rawls decommissioned 2026-07-31) — safe to delete once confirmed unused, no transition period left to preserve.
- **Bumping a Python container's interpreter version**: the Dockerfile's `FROM python:...` tag must exact-match the project's `.python-version`, or `uv sync` silently downloads its own managed interpreter as root and the non-root runtime user can't read it (this took down `research-queue` in prod — ETH-od5s9). Procedure + verification checklist: [`../docs/development/PYTHON-VERSION-BUMPS.md`](../docs/development/PYTHON-VERSION-BUMPS.md). If you're bumping the same container's version repeatedly, also read [`../docs/development/RUST-MIGRATION-SIGNALS.md`](../docs/development/RUST-MIGRATION-SIGNALS.md).

"""The git-tracked research stacks must not silently drop an environment variable.

ETH-wtshy. Rewriting a Coolify-era compose file by hand is the step where a
variable quietly disappears: the container still starts, the code takes a
different default, and nothing reports it. `PIPELINE_JOB_MAX_LLM_*=0` is the
sharp example -- those encode a CIO decision that LLM budgets are UNLIMITED
(ETH-wn0n8, 2026-08-03). Losing them would silently re-impose whatever the code
defaults to, on a production research queue, with no error anywhere.

So this asserts an exact partition, per service:

    inline `environment:` keys
  + keys listed in the env_file manifests the service references
  + keys deliberately dropped (each with a recorded reason)
  = exactly the key set the service carried on the live Coolify stack

Nothing is allowed to be merely absent. A key must be inline, in a manifest, or
explicitly dropped with a justification -- three places, all reviewable.
    assert vol["external"] is True
    assert vol["name"] == "y4xdlvh2oiq408ddgz6v92dd_research-defeatbeta-data", (
        "the defeatbeta parquet corpus lives here; a project-prefixed name would "
        "start the services on an EMPTY volume"
    )

    for net, want in {
        "coolify": "coolify",
        "research-app": "y4xdlvh2oiq408ddgz6v92dd",
    }.items():
        assert compose["networks"][net]["external"] is True
        assert compose["networks"][net]["name"] == want
    # The rawls stack's network was detached with its retirement (ETH-ycgxw.2.1).
    assert "/var/cache/searxng" in targets


@pytest.mark.parametrize("stack,alias", [("searxng", "searxng"), ("crawl4ai", "crawl4ai")])
def test_service_is_reachable_by_a_sane_name(stack, alias):
    """The reason both URLs went stale and stayed stale: the only resolvable name
    was a Coolify UUID, so there was nothing sensible to repoint them at."""
    doc = yaml.safe_load((RESEARCH_STACKS / stack / "docker-compose.yaml").read_text())
    svc = doc["services"][stack]
    assert alias in svc["networks"]["coolify"]["aliases"]

  - pipeline names `coolify_proxy_*` in cron_daemon_allowlist.py (their comments no longer point at scripts that are gone)

  - the kener DEAD_HOSTS and RETIRED_TAGS entries
  - the synthetic `COOLIFY_API_TOKEN` fixture in omni-anonymizer/tests/incident_corpus.py

**Checks** (failures marked pre-existing fail the same way on origin/main)

  - lint-workload-shape, lint_direct_deepinfra, lint-service-url-contract, lint-compose-env-contract, validate_project_metadata and lint-cron-registry all pass.
  - test_alert_state_deployment 4/4, email-triage test_model_defaults 8/8, kener tests 10/10.
  - The scripts/ci test group: 198 passed, 5 failed.
- **Pre-existing failures:**
  - Those 5: the 3 container cases in test_lint_deploy_secret_allowlist_containers, test_real_repo_is_clean, and test_hand_edit_of_the_snapshot_reds.
  - lint-deploy-secret-allowlist exits 2 because .forgejo/workflows/deploy.yml does not exist.
  - test_critical_crons: 2 failures caused by a wrong REPO_ROOT.
  - Combined critical-crons + critical-canaries run: 38 failed and 56 errors from collection and import problems, the same on both. 84 passed on the branch against 85 on main; the difference is the dropped canaries env case.
- **Outside my scope:** lint-service-url-contract suggests removing research/scripts/archive_evidence_to_r2.py from the crawl.ec1c.com baseline. That file belongs to another fork.
